Two intensities: Everyday keeps familiar interface fonts and small chisel details. Relic extends warped mineral fields and short branching fractures across the ribbon, tabs, sidebars, search header, menus, and status bar. Shared recessed joints, cut corners, and a single chisel seal connect its folders, title frames, properties, and action tablets. Reading and code fonts stay familiar in both. The base palette measurements are shared; texture-specific checks are in the material report; the stronger geometry and lettering still need your real-use judgment. Bold has its own rose-copper color again.

What the metric means, and the optical reasoning
  • Nominal text contrast checks the specified roles, surfaces, and active line at 4.5:1 or above. The filled buttons’ normal, hover, and pressed labels are checked, along with focus contrast. This is a component check, not a whole-app accessibility audit.
  • OKLab distance is a useful model for separating accents. It is not a guarantee that a colorblind observer can distinguish them, so weight, labels, underlines, icons, and focus rails remain useful.
  • Reading research examines contrast together with character size; small text cannot be judged from a color ratio alone. Native font rendering is checked separately, and Cairn is reserved for larger headings by default.
  • Polarity research does not establish a universally comfortable dark palette. This experiment follows your preference for Nord’s background; screen brightness, ambient light, viewing distance, and individual vision remain unmeasured.
  • Design cues: Nord’s cool surface ladder, Rosé Pine’s base/surface/overlay roles, and Catppuccin’s role-based text and accent hierarchy. The stone treatment and Hearthstone colors are custom.

Nord’s reported color-distance probe is not a compliance audit. Both panes are the same lightweight HTML mockup, with the respective theme stylesheet; they are not running Obsidian windows. “Match typography” helps isolate the color and material differences.
